references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus' mother and brothers come to speak with him, but the crowd prevents them from reaching him.
Parallel passage in Mark where Jesus' mother and brothers come and stand outside, sending for him because they cannot get in to him due to the crowd.
Mentions Jesus' mother and brothers by name, providing context for who the family members were that came to him.
Mentions Jesus' mother and brothers together, showing that they often followed him as a family group.
Jesus' brothers urge him to go to Judea, and the text notes that they did not believe in him, which may shed light on the motivation behind the family's visit in Luke 8:19.
After Jesus' ascension, his mother and brothers are gathered with the disciples in prayer, showing that the family eventually became part of the community of faith.
Paul mentions that he met James, the Lord's brother, in Jerusalem – this confirms that Jesus had brothers who became leaders in the early church.
